title: Operator Experimentation Lab and Incident Hypothesis Playbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary:

This playbook defines a lightweight, repeatable process for treating incidents as hypotheses and running short, instrumented experiments during low-impact windows (the "Operator Experimentation Lab"). The intent is to accelerate learning about failure modes, reduce blast radius through controlled shadow ops, and produce higher-quality postmortems with actionable remediation steps.

Scope and intended audience:
- Applies to oncall engineers, SREs, service owners, and platform operators across Redwood Inference.
- Focused on transient degradations, KV-cache regressions, routing fallbacks, and autoscaling edge cases. Not intended for full SEV1 outages that require immediate containment.

Key definitions:
- Experiment window: a scheduled 30–90 minute slot where controlled tests run against non-production or canary slices.
- Hypothesis incident: an observed signal with a testable root-cause hypothesis (e.g., "throttle surge + slow kernel selection causes >200ms tail in region-us-west2").
- Shadow ops: executing corrective or investigative actions in a non-customer-facing mode (mirror traffic, dark-launch toggles, non-committed rollouts).

When to use this playbook:
1) You have an incident signal below SEV1 where the triage team has time to validate a hypothesis (SLO regression <20% customer impact).
2) There is ambiguity in root cause and a short live test could disambiguate between causal factors (e.g., kernel choice vs. batching policy).
3) The service owner approves a shadow operation and there is a clear rollback path.

Operator Experimentation Lab checklist (pre-experiment):
1. Author hypothesis: one-sentence hypothesis and expected observable metric delta (e.g., "Expose quantized kernel v2 reduces p50 latency by 15% for seq_len<=512").
2. Scope traffic: select canary tenant(s) or synthetic traffic. Note tenant IDs or synthetic job IDs.
3. Impact assessment: estimate expected customer impact (tokens dropped, failed requests). If >5% chance of visible customer errors, abort.
4. Approval: service owner + oncall lead sign-off. Record in this doc: approvers and timestamp.
5. Safety hooks: monitoring alerts, automated rollback play, and circuit-breaker thresholds.
6. Runbook and observer assignment: owner for the experiment, observer(s) who will collect traces and evidence.

Experiment execution procedure (numbered steps):
1. Prepare environment: confirm canary routing, synthetic harness, and observability dashboards (latency, errors, cpu/gpu utilization, KV-hit-rate).
2. Baseline capture (T-10m): record key metrics for 10 minutes before change. Use /metrics/export job id or dashboard snapshot.
3. Apply change to canary (T0): annotate change in experiment log, note git commit/infra diff, and add a short tag to tracing.
4. Monitor (T0 to T+30m): continuous watch for degradations, collect flame graphs and kernel-level traces if tracing flags are enabled.
5. Quick decision gate (T+15m): if any safety hook trips, roll back immediately and proceed to containment notes.
6. Ramp / revert (T+30m): either ramp to additional canaries if safe, or revert and capture post-change metrics.
7. Evidence capture and synthesis: collect traces, heap profiles, kernel selection logs, and summarize in the experiment result section.

Templated experiment metadata (table-style listing to copy into incident ticket):
- experiment_id: OPX-YYYYMMDD-<short>
- hypothesis: <one sentence>
- owner: <name + pager>
- scope: <tenant IDs or synthetic jobs>
- baseline_snapshot: <dashboard link or metrics export id>
- commit/ref: <git sha or infra diff URL>
- start_time: <RFC3339>
- end_time: <RFC3339>
- safety_thresholds: <e.g., error_rate>0.5% OR latency_p95>1200ms>
- rollback_plan: <step list>

Runbook templates included (copyable snippets):
- Containment step (fast path):
  1) Disable canary routing: run "redwoodctl route set --service <svc> --route canary:false"
  2) Scale down new kernel pods: "kubectl scale deployment/<svc>-kernel --replicas=<prev> -n infra"
  3) Clear KV prefix cache if suspect: "redis-cli --eval scripts/evict_prefix.lua <prefix>"

- For autoscaler anomalies:
  1) Pin desired replicas: "kubectl patch hpa/<svc> -p '{\"spec\":{\"minReplicas\":X}}'"
  2) Force warm pool allocation: trigger "infra warmup --pool <pool-id> --count N"

Game-day design for experiments and shadow ops:
- Frequency: monthly 90-minute lab per team + quarterly cross-team coordination game-day.
- Attendees: oncall engineers, SRE, runtime team, product owner (optional), incident commander (rotating).
- Objectives: validate a single hypothesis end-to-end, practice safe rollback, measure time-to-evidence.
- Scoring: 1) did the experiment run to completion? 2) was rollback executed within threshold if required? 3) evidence quality (traces + repeatability).

Postmortem and hypothesis reporting requirements (minimums):
- One-line summary of what happened and whether hypothesis was supported.
- Evidence list: traces, metric diffs, kernel logs, commit ids.
- Remediation plan with owner and ETA (patch, config change, longer-term architecture).
- If experiment failed to discriminate, list next hypotheses and planned experiments.
- Attach experiment metadata table (above).

Rotation and staffing guidance for lab runs:
- Lab owner is the oncall lead for the week or designated lab coordinator.
- Observers: at least one SRE and one runtime engineer for kernel-level experiments.
- Paging policy: during lab windows, critical paging remains unchanged. Non-critical alerts may be muted with explicit approval.

Customer communications and status page templates (minimal safe language):
- Internal short blurb (to internal channels):
  "We observed an elevated p95 latency in region-us-west2. We are running a controlled canary experiment to validate a kernel optimization and will revert automatically if safety thresholds are hit. No customer-facing errors expected at this time."

- Public status page (concise):
  "Investigating: We are validating a mitigation for elevated inference latency in us-west2. Customer requests remain largely served; some requests may experience transient slower responses. We will provide updates in the next 30 minutes."

- Customer-sensitive template for enterprise tenants (CS/AE use):
  "We are investigating increased latency affecting a subset of requests in us-west2. Our engineering team is running a controlled canary to test a mitigation; we do not expect data exposure or request loss. We will share findings and mitigation ETA within 2 hours. If you see increased errors, please open a support ticket and reference OPX-<id>."

Measurement and observability checklist (metrics to capture):
- p50/p95/p99 latency (inference and backend), error rate, token drop rate, request throughput, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, kernel selection distribution, batching size histogram.
- Trace tags to include: experiment_id, canary=true, kernel_variant, tenant_id.

Decision gates and escalation ladder (quick reference):
1) If error_rate > 0.5% for 5m OR latency_p95 > SLA_threshold for 5m -> escalate to incident commander and rollback.
2) If resource saturation (GPU mem > 90% or OOMs) -> immediate rollback and page infra team.
3) If hypothesis supported and improvement >10% p95 with no safety trips -> schedule rollout plan and a postmortem write-up.

Ownership and follow-up cadence:
- Experiment owner must post a 2-paragraph summary and evidence to the incident ticket within 24 hours.
- Full postmortem (if experiment touched production or surfaced customer impact) due in 72 hours.
- Action items assigned in GH issues or internal tracker with owner and due date; engineering manager verifies closure during weekly triage.

Appendix A — Example incident-to-experiment flow (short narrative):
1) Signal: automatic SLO alert for p95 increases in us-west2.
2) Triage: oncall gathers traces, hypothesizes that new batching policy is increasing tail.
3) Decision: run experiment using shadow traffic vs. canary tenant; approved by service owner.
4) Experiment: change batching policy on canary, monitor 30 minutes, safety hooks OK.
5) Outcome: p95 improved 12% on canary, no increase in errors. Hypothesis supported.
6) Postmortem: schedule rollout with staged canaries and monitor.
